answers.answer: Herbicide application has mixed effects on Native plant cover and richness, based on 30 claims from 7 studies (per-study verdicts: 2 decrease, 3 increase, 1 mixed, 1 no effect). Example (Stover 2017): "In 2011 and 2012 native forb cover and richness were significantly lower with glyphosate than controls at Site 3; but only cover at Site 2 in 2011 and Site 3 in 2013 (Fig. 1)."

Mulch & surface cover has mixed effects on Invasive / non-native species abundance, based on 5 claims from 1 studies (per-study verdicts: 1 mixed). Example (Murphy 2007): "Significant differences are due to increases in exotic species in single treatments and decreases in extended treatments."

Peatland rewetting increases Methane emissions, based on 5 claims from 2 studies (per-study verdicts: 2 increase). Example (Wilhelm 2015): "Methane emissions from the experimental site were much greater (habitat: F(2, 18) = 18.8, p\0.0001), and unlike the reference plot increased substantially from 2008 to 2009 (year 9 habitat: F(2, 18) = 23.3, p\0.001) s..."

Nursery fertilization has mixed effects on Seedling growth, based on 52 claims from 11 studies (per-study verdicts: 6 increase, 2 mixed, 3 no effect). Example (Thiffaul 2010): "The use of herbicide significantly increased 15-year GLD and volume index of all three conifer species, but only black spruce responded positively to fertilization at planting."

Prescribed burning decreases Invasive / non-native species abundance, based on 3 claims from 2 studies (per-study verdicts: 2 decrease). Example (Stanley 2011): "Agrostis spp. were reduced most substantially by the SBG treatment (Figure 2b)."
The graph has no claim linking Mowing to Bird abundance.
